articles.title: Unofficial GTA 6 Worldwide Release Times Revealed, And The US Gets It Almost Last
articles.summary: GTA 6 is one of the most-anticipated games ever, and it arrives on November 19. People naturally want to know when exactly that day it will be available to play, and now it looks the like first indication of that has come to light.
body: GTA Vice scoured PlayStation Store listings for the game across 63 countries and regions, and discovered that the game will not have a global simultaneous release. It looks like the US will be among the last major markets to get it.
Again, this is all based on PlayStation Store listings and is not confirmed by Rockstar. GameSpot has followed up with the developer seeking comment.

According to GTA Vice, GTA 6 will unlock--on the PlayStation Store, at least--at midnight local time. That means people in New Zealand and Australia will get in first and the US will be among the final major regions to get started.

In short, GTA 6 will become available to play in New Zealand at midnight in the country, which works out to 5 AM PT / 8 AM ET on November 18. People in the US will then have to wait 16 hours to play GTA 6 where they live.
points: GTA 6 is one of the most-anticipated games ever, and it arrives on November 19.
People naturally want to know when exactly that day it will be available to play, and now it looks the like first indication of that has come to light.

articles.title: 'You Get Your Tariff Money back... if You Give Them More Money' — Fans React to Nintendo's 'Customer Appreciation' Sale
articles.summary: Fans are reacting to the announcement of a unique "Customer Appreciation" sale that Nintendo claims has been "made possible in part by tariff-related refunds." Nintendo will temporarily reduce the price of "dozens of Nintendo Switch digital games and bundles, plus savings on select physical games…
body: While cheaper prices are nothing to be sniffed at, the framing of this promotion — which runs for just two weeks, from September 13 through September 26 — as being funded by tariff refunds has certainly raised eyebrows.

Nintendo and numerous other companies are now recouping the money they previously handed over to the U.S. government as part of tariffs that have since been deemed illegal. Nintendo (and again, numerous other companies) raised prices to combat these tariffs, and fans have been calling for Nintendo to pass some of its tariff refund back to gamers. Indeed, a proposed class action lawsuit is brewing, calling for Nintendo to share its refund with Switch purchasers — but the company itself has argued that it has no reason to do so.

Today's sale announcement is being taken by some fans as a way to placate those fans who remain upset about all this, while also continuing to signal that it won't be doling out partial refunds to any recent Switch and Switch 2 customers.

articles.title: All match overrides and console locations in Fortnite Chapter 7 Season 4
articles.summary: Match overrides change the way you play Fortnite in Chapter 7 Season 4. Here are all the match overrides and where to find override consoles.
body: Match overrides allow you to change how Fortnite Chapter 7 Season 4 is played, but only if you interact with the override console first.

Luckily, override consoles will spawn in the same locations every game and they can be activated every game. However, only one override console will be activatable at a time, and it'll be activatable at a random time during the match. More override consoles can activate later on in a game, but the number will vary.

If you're the first person to interact with a console, you can choose between three match overrides, each of which will adjust the rules in your Fortnite game. These overrides can increase your sprint speed, give you more XP, make your pickaxes deal more damage, and much more. Some match overrides might also only affect your squad, rather than the entire lobby.
Below we've listed where you can find every override console in Fortnite Chapter 7 Season 4 and all the match overrides.

articles.title: Nintendo Announces New Switch Sale Made Possible By "Tariff-Related" Refunds
articles.summary: Nintendo has announced a new 'Customer Appreciation' Sale in the U.S, offering 30% off dozens of Switch games and more, starting on September 13 and running through September 26.
body: Select games, downloadable content, accessories, amiibo, and apparel will be discounted, although Nintendo has not yet provided a full list of the games and other products that will be included in the sale across the Nintendo eShop, Nintendo Store, and other participating retailers.

The video game giant has also said that the promotion is "made possible in part by tariff-related refunds". The company says it "absorbed most tariff-related costs", but the refunds have helped make promotions such as this new sale possible.

Nintendo previously faced questions over what it would do with money returned after the US tariff regime was challenged. Nintendo recently raised the prices of some Switch products globally, citing a combination of factors including tariffs, rising component costs, labour and shipping.

It subsequently argued that consumers were not entitled to refunds for purchases made at those higher prices after a court ruled the tariffs illegal. Nintendo said customers had received "exactly what they bargained and paid for" and that it was not required to retroactively adjust prices following the outcome of the tariff litigation.

articles.title: Iron Man: How [Spoiler]'s Shocking Return Changes Everything for Tony Stark
articles.summary: Iron Man writer Joshua Williamson breaks down the shocking return in issue #9 and how this major twist will upend Tony Stark's world in the months to come.
body: When Joshua Williamson took over Marvel’s relaunched Iron Man comic earlier this year, he immediately set about reinventing the franchise. Part of that involves exploring the central idea that Tony Stark’s mind, not Iron Man, is the real weapon to be feared. But there’s also one of the book’s biggest burning mysteries - who is the new Citizen V? Why has this villain returned, and who is under the mask this time?

Readers finally got an answer to that question in Iron Man #9. That chapter ends with the climactic reveal that Citizen V is none other than Tony’s former BFF and bodyguard, Happy Hogan. You didn’t see that coming?

This reveal comes as Iron Man and Citizen V square off against two versions of Whiplash, Mark Scarlotti and Anton Vanko. Citizen V offers himself up as a hostage in order to save the life of the son of Tony’s new girlfriend, Luna. As he unmasks, Happy notes that he’s not the only one Tony Stark left for dead.
points: Iron Man writer Joshua Williamson breaks down the shocking return in issue #9 and how this major twist will upend Tony Stark's world in the months to come.

articles.title: Nintendo’s Latest Sale Is Made Possible By Tariff Refunds It’s Not Giving You
articles.summary: Nintendo of America has announced a "Customer Appreciation Sale," offering 30% off games and access, with Nintendo specifically citing its tariff refunds as the reason why it's running the sale, at least in part.
body: "The Customer Appreciation Sale is our way of saying thank you to Nintendo players for their continued support and is made possible in part by tariff-related refunds. While Nintendo absorbed most tariff-related costs, the refunds helped make promotions like this one possible," the company said.

Nintendo, like Sony and Microsoft, got money back from the US government related to tariffs, which were implemented by US President Donald Trump and later deemed illegal by the Supreme Court. All three companies argued in court that they should keep the money and give nothing back because that's just how capitalism works.

The Customer Appreciation Sale runs September 13-26 on the Nintendo eShop, Nintendo Store, and select retailers. Items on sale vary by retailer, but shoppers can expect discounts on digital and physical games, DLC, accessories, Amiibo, and apparel.

Not every gaming company is taking such a hard line on this topic. Panic, the company behind the Playdate gaming handheld, said it will pass its own refunds on to customers who paid more. People should get about $12 back.

articles.title: Star Wars Zero Company Is Missing The Only Achievement I Wanted
articles.summary: Star Wars Zero Company released late last month, and it became one of my favorite games of the year almost instantly. I recently finished it, and while I was very satisfied with how it all wrapped up, there was one thing--a certain achievement--that was missing, and it filled me with a rage I can…
body: You see, like the XCOM series it took so much inspiration from, Star Wars Zero Company features a permadeath mechanic. With the exception of main protagonist Hawks, any of the allies you take into battle will permanently disappear if they're killed in battle.

Aside from accidentally knocking someone off the side of the map because I was still going through the tutorial segments in the first hour or so (I restarted the mission in this case), I managed to get through the entire game without losing anyone. Well, except for the poor fellow who automatically dies in the opening segment. The credits rolled and I waited for the achievement to pop up on my Xbox.

Indeed. There are achievements for everyone from making an almost-impossible shot to changing some cosmetic items, but there is no achievement for making it through the game without losing a squad member. There is, however, an achievement for having a squad member die on your watch. If you're on PlayStation, it's a literal participation trophy.

articles.title: A Top Boss At GTA 6 Company Take-Two Sold A Bunch Of Stock, But It’s Not What You Think
articles.summary: With Rockstar's GTA 6 on the horizon, and poised for massive success, many people might be interested in buying stock of Rockstar's parent company, Take-Two, as opposed to selling it.
body: A regulatory filing ( via The Motley Fool ) revealed that Goldstein sold 1,335 shares of Take-Two on September 2 at a price of $217.65. The total sale price worked out to $282,039. That's a fat stack of cash, but it was an automatic sell-to-cover sale to satisfy tax witholding obligations. Not very exciting stuff.

Following the sale of these 1,335 shares, Goldstein continues to hold a whopping 282,039 shares of Take-Two, which are worth more than $60 million on the open market. The value of those shares could climb significantly, as numerous stock analysts at big banks are projecting Take-Two's stock to grow significantly, with some saying it could go beyond $300 per share.

Take-Two currently trades at around $211/share, which is down more than 16% so far this year and down about 14% in the past 12 months. The company's share price got hammered in January after Google announced new AI tools for game development, and the stock price has not fully recovered.

articles.title: Nintendo of America thanks fans for dealing with tariff-related price hikes by encouraging them to spend more money in a new sale
articles.summary: Nintendo of America is currently facing a class action lawsuit for refusing to pass tariff refunds onto customers, and it's against that backdrop it today announced a "Customer Appreciation Sale" apparently made possible by those rebates.
body: In a blog post, Nintendo called this one of its "largest promotions ever", and included the following line which has had people scratching their heads: "While Nintendo absorbed most tariff-related costs, the refunds helped make promotions like this one possible."

A quick recap: following the introduction of tariffs by the current US government last year, Nintendo increased the price of multiple products in the country, citing "market conditions" as justification.

Nintendo, in this sale announcement, argues that it "absorbed" most of the costs, but the company has received a refund. The US consumers who bought Nintendo products since the price increase also suffered increased costs thanks to the tariffs, but they aren't receiving refunds. The reason this is rubbing people the wrong way is because Nintendo is thanking them for dealing with increased costs by encouraging them to spend more money.

The counter argument is, hey, why look a gift horse in the mouth? This is a discount on some games and peripherals at a time when buying new stuff in this market is awfully expensive. This ultimately could be seen as a gesture of goodwill, and one Switch owners could benefit from.

articles.title: Exclusive: Magic Designers Reveal the Evil Math Behind Reality Fracture — See 3 New Cards
articles.summary: Magic: The Gathering ’s upcoming set Reality Fracture is the culmination of a three-year plot arc and the 19-year story of Jace Beleren, the mind mage who has become one of the game’s most iconic characters.
body: Francis Tneh illustrated the Booster Fun version of the blue sorcery Cruel Calculations with a new frame called Sculptor’s Stronghold, which will appear on a total of 25 cards in the set. Executive producer Mike Turian tells Polygon the treatment is meant to demonstrate how Jace is watching over the Echoverse. The card is closely tied to the Theorix school at Hexhaven, the Echoverse’s twisted version of Strixhaven, which the Theorist uses as his base.

“This art for Cruel Calculations shows some of the inherent risks that come with the kind of forbidden reality-bending math and physics being taught in Theorix,” Reality Fracture narrative lead Meris Mullaley tells Polygon via email. “The best Theorix students can learn to bend reality, but for every elite student, there are many peers who failed their tests.”
The card is meant to synergize with Omit Variables, a prepared spell found on Theorix cards like the uncommon Paradox Shaper, which mills three cards for one black or blue mana.

articles.title: Avatar: Seven Havens Trailer Reveals the Fantasy Series’ Apocalyptic Future
articles.summary: Avatar Studios’ first production, Avatar Aang: The Last Airbender, picks up 13 years after the end of Avatar: The Last Airbender to give fans the chance to spend a bit more time with the beloved characters.
body: Avatar: Seven Havens takes place 225 years after the events of the first Avatar sequel, The Legend of Korra. Avatars can live far longer than a typical human lifespan, and the trailer shows a much older Korra with white-streaked hair seemingly unleashing fire and tentacles of spirit energy on a city in a fit of rage. The deed is memorialized in a mural depicting Korra in the Avatar state as a demonic figure.

That’s a big problem for the new Avatar, the Earthbender Pavi, a child even younger than Aang was at the start of his journey. Pavi lives in the city of Ellora, a metropolis tucked between canyons that protect it from constantly raging sandstorms and tornadoes. Kids there grow up learning to hate the Avatar for causing this cataclysm. But when the Airbender Jae is caught under rocks in a sandstorm, Pavi reveals she is the Avatar by using both Earthbending and Airbending.

articles.title: "What in the vibe-coded s*** is this" - RuneScape players revolt as gen-AI copycat game appears and eventually attracts the eye of Jagex
articles.summary: A clone of Old School RuneScape that appeared on the internet this week, and stoked the ire of the RuneScape community, has quickly been shut down.
body: The clone was made by e OpenAI employee Rohan Varma, who used the GPT-6 Astra to build a version of RuneScape he named Elderwood, which was playable in a browser.

In a video - itself created with gen-AI - uploaded to X, we see a character created and spawning outside Lumbridge castle, with an inventory of bread, coins, and basic tools. We then see the same character fighting giant rats, chopping trees, and equipping steel armour. It looks incredibly similar to Old School RuneScape save for a few inconsistencies..

But as Verma continued to experiment and share their progress on X, the posts caught the attention of the Old School RuneScape community who were displeased with what they found. In a thread posted to the 2007scape Reddit, users were not shy in their criticisms.

"What in the vibe coded shit is this. They even straight up ripped art assets shameless," wrote user RangeCreed. "Love the tweet format. AI bros can only speak in numbers and bullet lists (ideally both at once)," adds Lekamil, while X user Toppo simply summarised the situation with the following: "tl;dr garbage."
points: A clone of Old School RuneScape that appeared on the internet this week, and stoked the ire of the RuneScape community, has quickly been shut down.
